target.title: `before_agent_run` receives no input provenance; several producers never stamp it — internal wakes look like user input at the gate
target.body:
**Bug type:** Plugins / hooks
**Beta release blocker:** No

---

## Summary

Core's typed `InputProvenance` is never exposed on the `before_agent_run` hook event, and several
run producers never stamp it, so internal wakes are indistinguishable from user input at the only
input gate plugins have.

OpenClaw core already models input provenance as a typed, three-kind taxonomy:
`InputProvenance = { kind: "external_user" | "inter_session" | "internal_system", … }`
(`src/sessions/input-provenance.ts:8-18`). Core consumes it for display projection and
session-state events.

The `before_agent_run` gate hook — documented as the input gate that runs "after prompt
construction and before any model input" and can `block` a run before the model reads the
prompt — **does not receive it**. `PluginHookBeforeAgentRunEvent`
(`src/plugins/hook-types.ts:1092-1107`) exposes `prompt`, `messages`, `systemPrompt`,
`accountId`, `channelId`, `senderId`, `senderIsOwner`, and no provenance of any kind. The
field's own doc comment asserts the wrong thing:

```ts
/** The user's message that triggered this run. */
prompt: string;
```

The hook contract describes prompt as a user message even when the triggering run may have originated internally. Separately, several run producers never populate `inputProvenance` at all, so for those runs the information does not
exist anywhere to be exposed.

Consequence: a plugin on the only pre-model gate cannot answer "did a human send this?" It can
gate on *content* but not on *origin*, so internal system wakes and inter-session traffic cannot
be distinguished from end-user input, and unattended full turns are started for work no human
asked for.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a log-only plugin on `before_agent_run` that dumps the event keys and passes:

```js
export default {
  id: "provenance-probe",
  register(api) {
    api.on("before_agent_run", (event, ctx) => {
      console.log("[probe]", ctx.sessionKey, Object.keys(event));
      return { outcome: "pass" };
    });
  },
};
```

2. Trigger a run from each producer family: a real user message; a `sessions_spawn` subagent;
   an isolated cron run; a `sessions_send` inter-session message; a compaction-triggered run.
3. Observe the logged event keys.

## Expected behavior

The event carries authoritative provenance for every run — at minimum the existing
`InputProvenance.kind` — so a plugin can classify the trigger as `external_user`,
`inter_session`, or `internal_system` and decide pass/block accordingly.

## Actual behavior

No provenance field is present on any run. Every trigger looks the same at the gate. For the
producers listed below, provenance is not merely unexposed — it is never set:

| Producer (current main `661cf964`) | Sets `inputProvenance`? |
| --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-run-admission-phase.ts:246` | yes |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-request-preflight.ts:47` | yes |
| `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts:441` (voice) | yes |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts:99` | yes |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts` | **no** |
| `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts` | **no** |
| `src/agents/harness/compaction.ts` | **no** |

The gate itself runs on all three runner families — `cli-runner.ts:606`,
`embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-before-agent-run.ts:43`, `harness/lifecycle.ts:125` — so
this is *not* a gate-coverage bypass. The gate fires; it just fires blind.

## OpenClaw version

Reproduced on `2026.6.11` (`e085fa1`) and `2026.7.1-beta.5` (`b6387af`).
Source references above verified against current `main` @ **`661cf9644df5`** (2026-07-14).

## Operating system

Linux (x86_64)

## Model / Provider

Provider-independent — the defect is in the hook event contract, before any model call.

## Impact and severity

The gate is the documented place to stop a run *before token spend*. Without provenance, a
plugin cannot suppress internally-generated wakes, so unattended full turns run for work no
human requested. In our fleet this produced complete model turns whose own conclusion was that
no action was needed.

This is the mechanism under a long-standing report class. Note the ecosystem status accurately:
**#8299** (config to suppress sub-agent announce; documents ~60% prompt-compliance for
`ANNOUNCE_SKIP`), **#13911** (per-channel announce suppression) and **#64103** (session status
misleads agents into duplicate spawns) are **open**. #43802, #41235, #76443, #43095, #48784 are
**closed as completed** and #17442, #40863 **closed as not-planned** — cited as historical
context for the shape of the pain, not as live bugs.

Cooperative suppression (`ANNOUNCE_SKIP`, `NO_REPLY`, `REPLY_SKIP`) is prompt-trust only; #8299
documents that it is unreliable. A typed signal at the gate is the enforceable version of what
those requests are asking for.

## Relationship to #84405

**#84405 shipped and this issue does not re-litigate it.** `before_agent_run` is now wired into
the embedded runner (`attempt-before-agent-run.ts`), so the runner-coverage gap it described is
closed. We confirmed that on `661cf964` before filing. What remains is orthogonal: the hook now
runs everywhere and still cannot see *where the run came from*.

## Suggested direction

We believe a minimal fix would be to expose the existing `InputProvenance` on `before_agent_run`,
stamp the currently unstamped producers, and add fail-open coverage. We can provide additional
sanitized reproduction details if useful.

Offered as technical guidance for whoever picks this up, not as a specification:

1. **Stamp provenance at every producer** — set `inputProvenance` where runs are born, covering
the three currently verified unstamped families above: cron isolated runs, subagent spawn,
and compaction.
2. **Expose it on the hook event** as authoritative: add `inputProvenance?: InputProvenance` to
   `PluginHookBeforeAgentRunEvent`, and fix the `prompt` doc comment, which currently claims
   user origin unconditionally.
3. **Fail-open semantics, stated precisely.** Two separate obligations, and only the first is
   core's:
   - **Core** must never invent provenance it does not know, and must never block a run merely
     because provenance is absent. Absent ⇒ `undefined`, passed through as-is.
   - **Provenance-aware plugins** should fail open on missing, unknown, or malformed provenance —
     i.e. a plugin that gates on origin must treat "I can't tell" as "let it through."
   Core does **not** override an explicit plugin `block`. If a plugin deliberately returns
   `block`, the existing hook contract honours it, and that stays true — it has to, or the gate
   is not a gate. Fail-open is a property of the *reference plugin behaviour and the core default*,
   not an override that second-guesses plugin decisions.
4. **Adversarial test battery** proving (3): with an unstamped producer or malformed provenance,
   core passes `undefined` without inventing a classification, and a provenance-aware reference
   plugin treats missing or malformed provenance as unknown and passes the run. Existing
   fail-closed behavior for throwing handlers or invalid plugin decisions should remain unchanged
   and be covered by regression tests.

## One implementation note, learned the hard way

A caution for whoever implements this: **a green test suite is not evidence of producer coverage.**
In local experimentation we stamped every producer we could find by reading the source, watched
the tests pass, and then found at runtime that we had still missed producer sites — because the
thing you get wrong is not the stamping, it is *which producers exist*. Whatever the fix looks
like, we would suggest verifying it against live runs from every dispatch family rather than
against offline coverage alone.
